# ActionMesh

> Typed TypeScript action contracts for AI tools, MCP-style calls, HTTP and CLI with shared Zod validation, errors and retry semantics.

## Canonical sources

- Repository: https://github.com/yashkhou/actionmesh
- Documentation: https://yashkhou.com/projects/actionmesh
- Releases: https://github.com/yashkhou/actionmesh/releases
- Issues: https://github.com/yashkhou/actionmesh/issues
- License: MIT

## What it is

ActionMesh is a framework-agnostic TypeScript action registry that keeps an operation’s input schema, output schema, implementation, errors and retry semantics in one contract.

## What problem it solves

The same capability is often reimplemented for agents, HTTP, CLI and MCP-style tools. ActionMesh keeps one action contract and makes those surfaces thin adapters.

## Key topics

mcp, model-context-protocol, ai-agents, agent-tools, tool-calling, typed-actions, zod, schema-validation, http-api, cli, typescript, developer-tools

## Frequently asked questions

### What is ActionMesh?
ActionMesh is a framework-agnostic TypeScript action registry that keeps an operation’s input schema, output schema, implementation, errors and retry semantics in one contract.

### Why use ActionMesh instead of separate handlers?
It reduces drift between agent tools, HTTP routes, CLI commands and MCP-style surfaces by keeping business logic in one action implementation and treating transports as adapters.

### Does ActionMesh implement the official MCP transport?
The current release ships an MCP-style listTools/callTool adapter. An official Model Context Protocol SDK transport is a separate roadmap item.

### What validates ActionMesh inputs?
ActionMesh uses Zod schemas for runtime input validation and can also validate outputs before returning them to callers.

Canonical technical authority: repository source code, tests, README, and tagged releases.
